# ADR-062 — Checkpoint 9.0: every retrying queue has a DLQ; occurrences failures durable through the alert router; 404s drop their query; OAuth state swept

**Status:** Locked

<!-- Decision text below is verbatim from the pre-split docs/DECISIONS.md table row (2026-09-16). Do not edit a Locked decision without explicit owner approval. -->

**Checkpoint 9.0 — every retrying queue has a dead-letter queue; occurrences failures are durable through the alert router; unknown routes drop their query; OAuth state is swept by retention (2026-09-12, owner-directed).** Phase 9 opens with a bounded reliability/privacy checkpoint rather than product work, closing the four items ADR-061 carried forward. **1. OCCURRENCES DEAD-LETTER CONTRACT.** `occurrences.generate-lazy` and `occurrences.expand-window` gain `.dead` queues attached by the 8.6A `createQueue → createQueue(deadLetter) → updateQueue` sequence in every process that creates them (api and worker for generate-lazy; worker for expand-window), because `create_queue` is `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` and both rows already existed in production. **Durable failure evidence is the notification router, not a column.** `occurrences.status` and `tasks.status` are CHECKed closed vocabularies with no jsonb, so no zero-migration column exists, and the checkpoint held migrations at zero; `notification_dispatch_log.dedupe_key` is the one permanent, never-swept table already built for exactly this. The keys follow ADR-058: `occurrences.generate-lazy.dead:<occurrenceId>` (the source occurrence IS the failure's identity; a later completion is a new failure and alerts again) and `occurrences.expand-window.dead:<UTC date of the dead job's own created_on>` (a global sweep changes nothing durable on failure, so a date bucket alerts once per night and re-arms — the `all_streams_failed` precedent; the DEAD job's `created_on` rather than the source's because pg-boss 12.27.0 drops `source_created_on` when the dead job itself is retried, which would mint two keys for one failure). The record presupposes ≥1 alert-eligible device, exactly as every existing alert producer does, and the structured log line is emitted regardless. **The generate-lazy dead handler is idempotent on CURRENT state and makes ONE further attempt** (state re-checks first; the realistic cause of exhausting five backoff retries is a transient outage that has healed; a 23505 is success), alerting only if that attempt throws, with the owner's task title — control-stripped, capped — in the body and ids only in `data`. **expand-window gains per-parent containment**: one throwing rule no longer aborts every parent after it; the contained error carries counts and a bounded (≤20) list of failed parent ids, never raw error text; the sweep is retried whole (idempotent via `onConflictDoNothing`) and its dead handler re-logs the failed ids so they survive a container recreation. The dead queues have no dead letter of their own: exhaustion THERE is terminal and logged. Guards test RUNTIME configuration — a real pg-boss booted against a queue that pre-exists WITHOUT a dead letter — in both processes, and the containment guard strips comments before matching so it cannot be satisfied by prose. **2. THE 404 LOGGING CONTRACT.** Fastify's `basic404` logged `Route <method>:<raw url> not found` as a plain message — bypassing the only serializer that scrubs `?code=`/`&state=`/`?q=` — and echoed the raw URL in the body. A `setNotFoundHandler` replaces it entirely. Policy: **a KNOWN route keeps name-based scrubbing** (its parameters are enumerable and diagnostic); **an UNKNOWN route, every `OPTIONS` request (served by `@fastify/cors`'s `OPTIONS *` catch-all, so never `is404`), and a malformed URL (`frameworkErrors`) lose the ENTIRE query** — `/path?[redacted]` — because a mistyped path can carry any parameter name and nothing would have read it. Method, path and a `route_not_found` / `malformed_request_url` classification remain. `#` is honoured as a query delimiter because find-my-way treats it as one. The 404 body is the API's own `{ error: "not_found" }`. Proven live: four sentinels, zero occurrences in the api log. **3. HRV, AND WHAT A SPEC MISMATCH NOW LEAVES BEHIND.** ADR-047's breaker behaved exactly as designed — five identical loud failures, zero rows stored, one alert — and is reaffirmed. The declaration was the catalog unit string mistaken for a field name. The shape was re-observed by a **read-only, value-free probe** (field names and JSON kinds only) and corrected to the documented `averageHeartRateVariabilityMilliseconds` with the deep-sleep RMSSD in the allowlisted breakdown; three further unobserved specs were corrected to their documented names and stay `observed: false`; `daily-sleep-temperature-derivations` is left deliberately non-matching because the documented field is an absolute temperature while the product's display key is a signed delta — an owner decision, not a spec typo. **A run row now records WHICH shape was rejected** (code as a token in `error_message`; `{code, keyPath, sawType, count}` in a value-free log line), so the next wrong declaration is diagnosable from the row rather than by a production probe. Re-enable ordering is load-bearing: the breaker reads the last five runs, so a stream is re-enabled only after the corrected worker is serving. **4. OAUTH STATE IS SWEPT, AND THE API FUNCTIONS ARE GONE.** ADR-047 recorded the intent; ADR-057 #1 and ADR-061 recorded that nothing called the two `apps/api` functions. They are deleted, and the cleanup is two further independent DELETEs in the existing daily `retention.cleanup` — **on the row's own `expires_at < now`, with no window constant** (the row carries its 10-minute TTL; an age window would be a second invented number), `consumed_at` not consulted. A live in-flight state has `expires_at` strictly in the future and cannot match; a deleted expired row changes only which `InvalidStateError` message a later consume throws. Irreversible under ADR-024, which is reaffirmed. The 8.6C windows are byte-unchanged. **Present-state corrections, in the ADR-057 convention:** ADR-047's sweep clause is now true in both halves; ADR-057 #1's OAuth-state half and ADR-061's "both sweep functions still unwired" and "`occurrences.*` retry with no DLQ" are closed; ADR-061's HRV item is closed. **Two gaps found by this checkpoint's own review are recorded, not fixed:** `PATCH /tasks/:id` seeds a lazy occurrence only on an anchor change, so "edit the rule" does not repair a dead-lettered successor; and `POST /occurrences/:id/complete|skip` with pg-boss down returns 200 and silently never generates the successor — a loss no DLQ can see because no job exists. **No migration** — level stays 17. **Phase 9's product theme is not decided by this ADR** (Checkpoint 9.0, 2026-09-12)
